At 0% progress, prioritize **controlled random-prefix truncation training for NextItNet**, supported by padding and history-sensitivity diagnostics. This is a proposed experiment; no improvement has been measured.

**Starting-point insights.** (1) Feedback implicates broad relevance and stale interests; recent-context reliance is a hypothesis, not established intent. (2) Training-pair margins depend on score scale and cannot establish ranking improvements. (3) Left padding requires final-nonpadding readout, never count−1; intermediate padding behavior also needs verification.

**Related-work insights.** (1) NextItNet’s causal convolutions provide a calculable receptive field [1]. Count every temporal convolution: R=1+Σ(k−1)d; the supplied schedule remains unverified. (2) CL4SRec already uses cropping [4], limiting novelty; DuoRec and EC4SRec warn that augmentation can disrupt semantics [5,6]. (3) Shuffling motivates behavioral controls [2], while sampled-metric bias limits conclusions to the pinned benchmark [3].

**Framework and directions.** Implementation correctness → padding/readout audits; temporal reliance → prefix interventions; supervision effects → matched-mask controls; predictive usefulness → fixed-candidate validation with popularity/history-length strata. Sensitivity alone establishes neither beneficial personalization nor causal intent.

**Candidate ideas.** Scores are originality/potential/difficulty, each 0–10; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

| Idea | Algorithm and reference | Scores | Positive / negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Padding-safe residual blocks | Audit leading-padding invariance; mask padding after temporal blocks if needed [1,7]. | 2/7/2 | Originality: targeted adaptation / established technique. Potential: dependable foundation / gains require a defect. Difficulty: local edits / predictor must match. |
| Controlled random-prefix truncation | Occasionally remove older context; compare against identical target masks without removal [1,4–6]. | 2/6/4 | Originality: NextItNet-specific controlled study / cropping is established. Potential: inexpensive robustness / useful long-term context may disappear. Difficulty: small transformation / controls require careful alignment. |
| Learned dilation gates | Jointly train scalar residual gates [1]. | 4/6/5 | Originality: adaptive context combination / familiar gating. Potential: flexible span / gates may collapse. Difficulty: modest architecture change / predictor and checkpoints change. |

**Selected experiment.** Retain the inexpensive truncation idea, but isolate context removal from supervision changes. Predeclare probability 0.25 and uniformly sampled retained lengths 8–32, clipped to available history; these remain unvalidated hypotheses. Report actual retained lengths, supervised-target counts, and their relation to R.

```text
A: intact inputs; baseline valid-target loss
B: intact inputs; sampled suffix target mask
C: same inputs, targets, negatives and suffix mask as B;
   additionally zero older input positions without shifting
retain original successors and immediate predecessors
optimize the same loss, normalized by valid-target count
```

A→B measures supervision redistribution; B→C isolates context removal. Match sampled users, target identities, negatives and optimizer steps between B/C. Separately compare all-position and final-position loss under identical contexts if budget permits. Preserve causal inputs; targets must never enter their own receptive fields.

Evaluate intact histories with identical pinned candidates. Select solely by macro validation HR@10; report category scores and paired user-bootstrap macro differences [8]. One extra hit changes category HR by 0.005 and macro HR by 0.00125. Bootstrap intervals exclude adaptive-selection, training-seed and candidate-sampling uncertainty [9]. Log every attempt and predeclare the affordable comparison budget.

Retain one model/checkpoint per category, seed 42, at most 200 epochs, 200 batches/epoch, preprocessing seed 0, routing, splits and DATA_DIR. Preserve both diagnostic APIs, ModelView, trial-local artifacts and embedded-predictor consistency. Report valid counts and unavailable measurements explicitly. Cropping may encourage short-context shortcuts; intact-versus-perturbed validation comparisons and history-length strata help detect this, without changing the evaluator.

idea.description: Evaluate random-prefix truncation within the supplied NextItNet using matched supervision controls. Train exactly one independent model per category in each experimental condition; compare conditions without combining their predictions or checkpoints.
idea.motivation: Qualitative feedback suggests older or isolated interactions may distract from coherent recent behavior, but does not establish current intent or satisfied needs. Cropping has established precedents, so the contribution is a controlled test of whether removing older accessible context improves this benchmark beyond changes in target weighting or supervision volume.
idea.implementation_notes: Use three predeclared conditions: A uses intact inputs and baseline supervision; B uses intact inputs with sampled suffix target masks; C uses the same masks as B and additionally removes older input context. In B/C, independently select rows with probability 0.25 and uniformly draw an integer retained length from 8 through 32, clipped to available nonpadding input length. For selected rows, retain original positions at or after the resulting cutoff; do not compact or shift. Preserve each retained target's original next-item alignment and immediate predecessor. Intersect the suffix mask with baseline valid-target positions. Generate B/C masks through a dedicated seeded augmentation RNG so augmentation does not change user, target or negative sampling; use matching initial weights, batch streams and optimizer steps. Use the identical baseline loss formula with explicit valid-target normalization; B/C must have identical denominators. Skip empty supervised batches consistently. A/B comparisons measure the combined effect of reduced and redistributed supervision, not a pure target-weighting effect. Each condition trains its own models from the supplied cold start; no checkpoints from other trials are reused, and no conditions are fused at inference. Bound this study by the remaining shared 43,200 GPU-second budget, counting controls, diagnostics and failures; defer optional all-position versus final-position comparisons if unaffordable. Before interpreting cropping, verify the baseline's actual dilation schedule, temporal convolutions, normalization axes, causality and padding behavior. Compute R = 1 + sum((kernel_width - 1) * dilation) over every stride-one temporal convolution; this describes accessible context only when other operations do not mix time globally. Leading-padding invariance requires preserving all real interactions and disabling dropout. For equal-length prefix interventions, changes strictly outside the receptive field should leave final features unchanged under position-local operations. Nonzero padded intermediate states can invalidate assumptions about replacing real prefixes with padding; audit them rather than assuming zero embeddings suffice. If padding fixes are necessary, apply them consistently to all conditions and update the embedded predictor. Evaluate intact left-padded histories at their final nonpadding position, normally L-1; never use nonpadding_count-1. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), and all other host ModelView interfaces. Do not invent unavailable categories, reviews, compatibility labels or user traits. Report undefined diagnostics as unavailable, with valid counts. Keep four-category routing, DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, at most 200 epochs and 200 batches per epoch. Preserve splits, negative candidates, evaluator and checkpoint/predictor consistency. Select only by the prescribed macro validation HR@10. If the host exposes per-user validation hits, bootstrap paired user indices within each category and average four category differences equally; otherwise do not claim an interval. Predeclare configuration and checkpoint-selection rules and log every attempted condition. Intervals for selected winners do not correct validation-selection bias. Monitor history-length and training-popularity strata and intact-versus-perturbed behavior for short-context shortcuts. These remain exploratory diagnostics, not evidence of ownership, replacement needs or causal intent.
idea.pseudocode:
conditions = ['A_full', 'B_mask_only', 'C_crop_and_mask']
# Run conditions separately from the supplied cold start; never fuse models.
for condition in conditions:
    reset_training_seed(42)
    model, optimizer = supplied_nextitnet_cold_start()
    batch_rng = dedicated_baseline_rng(seed=42)
    augmentation_rng = dedicated_augmentation_rng(seed=42)
    for step in prescribed_training_steps:
        sequence, positive, negative = baseline_sample_batch(batch_rng)
        valid = baseline_valid_target_mask(sequence, positive)
        suffix_mask = ones_like(valid)
        cropped_sequence = sequence.clone()
        # Generate the same augmentation schedule in every condition.
        for b in rows(sequence):
            occupied = nonzero_positions(sequence[b])
            crop_row = augmentation_rng.uniform() < 0.25
            if crop_row and len(occupied) > 0:
                s = min(augmentation_rng.randint_inclusive(8, 32), len(occupied))
                cutoff = occupied[-s]
                suffix_mask[b, :cutoff] = False
                cropped_sequence[b, :cutoff] = 0
        inputs = cropped_sequence if condition == 'C_crop_and_mask' else sequence
        supervised = valid if condition == 'A_full' else (valid & suffix_mask)
        if not supervised.any():
            continue
        features = model.log2feats(inputs)
        loss = baseline_loss_with_explicit_valid_normalization(
            features, positive, negative, supervised)
        optimizer.zero_grad()
        loss.backward()
        optimizer.step()
# B and C share target identities, negatives, masks and loss denominators.
# Evaluate every condition with intact histories and final-nonpadding readout.
# Host selection uses unchanged four-category macro validation HR@10.
# Each category predictor loads exactly one trained model/checkpoint.

originality.positive: The matched-mask comparison gives a precise NextItNet-specific test separating context removal from altered supervision.
originality.negative: Random cropping and subsequence training have clear precedents; neither cropping nor the proposed controls establish a novel model class.

future_potential.positive: A controlled finding could motivate context selection inside one jointly trained NextItNet and clarify when older history helps.
future_potential.negative: Benefits may be benchmark-specific regularization; random removal can discard useful semantics and encourage excessive reliance on recent items.

code_difficulty.positive: The intervention is a small batch transformation and adds no inference component.
code_difficulty.negative: Reproducible matched sampling, loss normalization, padding audits and multiple training controls require more work and GPU budget than the original sampler-only description suggested.

related_work.title: [1] NextItNet
contributions: Introduces causal dilated convolutions and residual blocks for sequential recommendation.
Provides the architectural basis for reasoning about accessible history spans.
limitations: Does not establish that prefix truncation improves this benchmark.
The supplied baseline's actual convolutions must be checked before calculating its receptive field.

related_work.title: [2] Does It Look Sequential?
contributions: Motivates sequence-shuffling controls and examination of ranking quality and recommendation overlap.
limitations: Perturbation sensitivity alone establishes neither useful personalization nor current intent.
Does not validate the proposed augmentation on the four supplied categories.

related_work.title: [3] On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled recommendation metrics can differ systematically from full-catalog metrics.
limitations: Does not justify changing the pinned evaluator.
Does not predict whether the proposed modification improves sampled validation HR@10.

related_work.title: [4] CL4SRec
contributions: Uses cropping, masking and reordering to construct contrastive sequence views alongside next-item learning.
Establishes a clear precedent limiting claims of originality for random cropping.
limitations: Its contrastive-view setting differs from supervised all-position NextItNet training.
Does not isolate context removal from the supervision changes in this proposal.

related_work.title: [5] DuoRec
contributions: Motivates avoiding semantic inconsistency from data augmentation through dropout views and same-target positive sequences.
limitations: Does not establish that every prefix crop changes semantics.
Its contrastive method is not implemented in the selected experiment.

related_work.title: [6] EC4SRec
contributions: Motivates importance-guided sequence augmentation because random transformations can remove useful information.
limitations: Does not supply validated item-importance estimates for this benchmark.
Importance-guided augmentation would add implementation and diagnostic complexity.

related_work.title: [7] RecBole NextItNet implementation
contributions: Provides an explicit example of causal left padding, residual blocks and channel normalization.
Illustrates why receptive-field calculations must count actual convolution dilations.
limitations: Its dilation schedule cannot be assumed to match the supplied corrected baseline.
Causal padding does not by itself guarantee zero intermediate padding states.

related_work.title: [8] SciPy paired bootstrap documentation
contributions: Documents paired resampling semantics applicable to matched per-user model outcomes.
limitations: The proposed category-stratified macro bootstrap requires an explicitly implemented aggregation procedure.
User resampling does not capture training-seed variation, candidate-sampling uncertainty or adaptive selection bias.

related_work.title: [9] On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: Explains how optimizing a finite-sample selection criterion can produce selection bias.
limitations: Does not quantify the bias for this particular search.
Predeclaring a modest search limits opportunities for overfitting but does not eliminate selection bias.

related_work.title: Official NextItNet implementation
contributions: Documents subsequence construction and differences in training-example counts.
Reinforces the need to control supervision volume when evaluating cropping.
limitations: Does not verify the supplied host implementation or establish the proposed experiment's outcome.
